# Embedding engine conventions (parent-owned — do not edit)

Every subagent working on the bge-m3 embedding engine (embedding_model_plan.md) MUST
follow these rules. They exist so independently-developed components integrate without
conflicts. Read `embedding_model_plan.md` and this file before writing any code.

## Ownership rule

Touch ONLY the files listed in your task prompt. Never edit: `examples/xmake.lua`,
`examples/CMakeLists.txt`, `examples/embedding/xmake.lua`,
`examples/embedding/CMakeLists.txt`, `src/tests/xmake.lua`,
`src/tests/CMakeLists.txt`, `examples/embedding/CONVENTIONS.md`, another agent's
sources, or anything under `src/tests/data/embedding/` (generated by the parent).
Build registration for your targets is ALREADY DONE — do not add or modify targets.

## Layout & namespace

- Engine code: namespace `luisa::embed`, headers `examples/embedding/embed/*.h`,
  sources `examples/embedding/embed/*.cpp`, kernels under `embed/kernels/`.
- Tests include engine headers as `#include "embedding/embed/xxx.h"` (the include
  root `$(projectdir)/examples` is already configured).
- Host-only engine code (tokenizer, package loader) must not include lc-dsl device
  headers; kernels must not leak into host-only headers.

## Style (cpp-style skill)

- C++20. NO exceptions, NO RTTI (`typeid`/`dynamic_cast` forbidden), no `std::` STL
  containers in engine code — use `luisa::vector`, `luisa::string`, `luisa::span`,
  `luisa::unique_ptr` from `<luisa/core/...>`. `std::filesystem::path` is allowed for
  API paths; `<cmath>` free functions are fine.
- Fatal errors: `LUISA_ERROR(...)` (noreturn). Warnings: `LUISA_WARNING(...)`.
- Every file starts with a short header comment: purpose + plan section reference.
- No `../../` includes; no `must(...)` in tests (this repo's Boost.UT has only
  `expect`). No `add_debug_checks`, no `LUISA_AST_DEBUG_KERNEL` in committed code.

## Kernel conventions (plan §4)

- Kernels are DSL `Kernel1D/2D` lambdas built device-free and returned from factory
  functions, compiled by the caller via `device.compile(...)`, cached as `Shader`
  objects by the eventual Session (Phase B). Factory pattern:

  ```cpp
  // embed/kernels/kernels_gemm.h
  #pragma once
  #include <luisa/dsl/...>
  namespace luisa::embed {
  // gemm: C[M,N] = epilogue(A[M,K] @ B[K,N] + bias)
  [[nodiscard]] auto make_gemm_kernel() noexcept;  // returns Kernel2D
  }
  ```

  Implementation in the matching `.cpp`. Keep each kernel's math next to a comment
  mapping it to the ONNX ops it replaces (see plan §4 table).
- `set_block_size(...)` explicit on every kernel. `dispatch(n)` = total threads.
  Grids that can exceed 65535 blocks must be flattened to 2D (DX limit).
- DSL runtime control flow only (`$if`, `$while`, `$for`); plain C++ loops only for
  fixed compile-time unrolls. Shared memory ≤ 32 KiB per block.
- fp32 everywhere in Phase A; explicit accumulators.
- Host-side CPU reference implementations used by tests follow the
  `examples/ml/attention_cpu_reference.{h,cpp}` pattern (naive triple loop, fp32,
  same math order as the ONNX graph, e.g. Erf-GELU: `0.5*x*(1+erf(x/sqrt(2)))`).

## Test conventions

- Boost.UT (`#include <boost/ut.hpp>`), `expect(...)` only; accumulate mismatches
  then `expect(count == 0u)`; float compares with tolerance, never `==`.
- Every test file starts with a header comment block: what it covers, plan §, how to
  run (`xmake run <target> dx`).
- Device tests: `luisa::test::create_device(argc, argv)` from `"test_device.h"`
  (backend = argv[1]: `dx`, `vk`, `cuda`, `fallback`). Run on `dx` first; also run
  `fallback`. Compare against a naive CPU reference computed in the test and report
  max-abs-diff / cosine in the log (`LUISA_INFO`) on every gate.
- Test data dir: macro `LUISA_EMBED_TEST_DATA_DIR` (absolute path, already defined).
  Goldens formats are described in `golden_meta.json` (read it). corpus.txt escapes
  `\` `\\n` `\\r` — unescape after reading a line.
- Host-only tests are marked `LUISA_EMBED_HOST_ONLY=1` and take no backend argument;
  they must run with zero device usage.

## Build & run (per-agent isolation — REQUIRED)

Each agent uses its OWN xmake output dir; never run bare `xmake f`/`xmake build`
without `-o build/embed_<id>` (it would clobber the shared config other agents use):

```
xmake f -p windows -a x64 -m debug -y -o build/embed_a3
xmake build -o build/embed_a3 <target> [<target> ...]
xmake run -o build/embed_a3 <test_target> dx
```

(`-o` may be omitted after the first config; xmake remembers it per-invocation only
when the working dir has .xmake state — safest is to always pass `-o`.)

After creating a NEW source file under `embed/`, re-run the `xmake f` line once so
the wildcard picks it up, then build. Build ONLY your own targets. The pack tool
target is `example_embed_pack_model`; the engine lib is `lc-example-embedding`.

Config note: this tree configures with clang-cl + `lc_win_runtime=MD` (scripts/
options.lua) — do not change project options. Debug mode is the dev leg; the parent
runs the release-mode review gate afterwards.

## Definition of done (report back)

1. Build log snippet: `xmake build` of your targets, zero errors, no new warnings.
2. Test run logs on `dx` AND `fallback` (device tests) or plain run (host-only),
   with the parity numbers (max-abs-diff / cosine) printed by the tests.
3. List of files created/modified (must match your ownership list exactly).
4. Any deviation from the plan, with reason.
